# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Comin_2025_glibenclamide"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Comin_2025_glibenclamide"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-025-01562-9> (open access, PMC12618397)

Comin et al. fitted a population PK model, in Monolix, to whole-body dynamic
PET data acquired over 40 min after an intravenous microdose of
[11C]glibenclamide (glyburide; the INN is used here). Concentrations were
derived from the image radioactivity in arterial blood, liver, kidneys, spleen
and pancreas. Each volunteer was scanned once with the tracer alone and, in 10
of 16, a second time immediately after a 30-min intravenous infusion of
rifampicin 9 mg/kg, which inhibits hepatic OATP uptake transporters.

# Population

Sixteen healthy volunteers (11 men, 5 women) were enrolled in three groups
(Comin 2025 Table 1): men older than 50 years (n = 4, median age 59 years,
range 50-64; median weight 81 kg), women older than 50 years (n = 5, 60 years,
59-65; 66 kg) and men younger than 30 years (n = 7, 25 years, 20-30; 73 kg).
One woman homozygous for the SLCO1B1 c.521T>C variant (CC genotype) was
excluded from model building, so the final model was fitted to 15 subjects;
Supplementary Table S1 refits the same model with her included. One man had
undergone a splenectomy and contributed no spleen data. The injected microdose
was 12.5 +/- 6.2 ug.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Comin_2025_glibenclamide")()$population`.

# Model structure

Results equation 5 and Figure 3 of the paper. All states are amounts (ug);
`central` is blood.

* `central` (blood, volume `vc`) exchanges first-order with `liver`, `kidney`,
  `spleen` and `pancreas` and is the only site of elimination (`kel`).
* `liver` exchanges with a catenary `liver_deep` sub-compartment; `kidney`
  likewise with `kidney_deep`. Each organ is observed as the **sum** of its two
  sub-compartments divided by one organ volume (`v_liver`, `v_kidney`).
* The dose enters blood as a zero-order input of estimated duration Tk0
  (`d1` = 0.015 h, about 54 s), so dose records use `rate = -2`.
* Rifampicin (`CONMED_RIFAMPICIN_SD = 1`) multiplies the liver-to-blood rate
  constant `k_liver_central` by `exp(0.96)` = 2.61.
* Inter-occasion variability (`OCC` = 1 or 2) is on `k_liver_central` only,
  with its SD fixed at 0.01.

# Derived quantities stated in the paper

The Results and Discussion quote several quantities that follow directly from
the Table 2 estimates. They are recomputed here from the packaged model; the
two sides are the same arithmetic, so the tolerances only absorb the paper's
rounding.

```{r derived}
mod <- readModelDb("Comin_2025_glibenclamide")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta

cl <- exp(th[["lvc"]]) * exp(th[["lkel"]])
k_lb <- exp(th[["lk_liver_central"]])
k_lb_rif <- k_lb * exp(th[["e_conmed_rifampicin_sd_k_liver_central"]])
k_bl <- exp(th[["lk_central_liver"]])
k_kb <- exp(th[["lk_kidney_central"]])
k_bk <- exp(th[["lk_central_kidney"]])
v_tissue <- exp(th[["lv_liver"]]) + exp(th[["lv_kidney"]]) +
  exp(th[["lv_spleen"]]) + exp(th[["lv_pancreas"]])

derived <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~model, ~paper, ~where,
  "CL = VB x ke (L/h)", cl, 2.84, "Results",
  "kL1B with rifampicin (1/h)", k_lb_rif, 55, "Results; Discussion",
  "kL1B / kBL1, no rifampicin", k_lb / k_bl, 2.3, "Results",
  "kK1B / kBK1", k_kb / k_bk, 2.9, "Results",
  "kBL1 / kL1B, no rifampicin", k_bl / k_lb, 0.43, "Discussion",
  "kBL1 / kL1B, with rifampicin", k_bl / k_lb_rif, 0.16, "Discussion",
  "Sum of organ volumes except blood (L)", v_tissue, 3.3, "Discussion"
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - paper) / paper)

derived |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity, "Model" = model, "Paper" = paper,
    "Paper location" = where, "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 3, 2, 0, 1))

stopifnot(all(abs(derived$pct_diff) < 5))
```

# Typical-value profiles (Figure 4)

Figure 4 of the paper shows individual fits for three subjects in each tissue
on both occasions. The typical-value predictions below show the same pattern:
the blood peak at the end of the short input followed by a rapid fall, liver
concentrations still rising at 40 min, kidney peaking at about 10 min, and fast
blood equilibrium in spleen and pancreas. Rifampicin roughly halves the liver
concentration and raises blood, kidney, spleen and pancreas concentrations a
little.

```{r typical}
dose_ug <- 12.5
t_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3 / 60, by = 10 / 3600), seq(3 / 60, 40 / 60, by = 2.5 / 60))))

make_events <- function(ids, occ, rif) {
  dose <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose_ug, rate = -2, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = t_obs) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(OCC = occ, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN_SD = rif) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  make_events(1L, occ = 1L, rif = 0L) |> mutate(occasion = "Baseline"),
  make_events(2L, occ = 2L, rif = 1L) |> mutate(occasion = "Rifampicin")
)

tissues <- c(Cc = "Blood", Cliver = "Liver", Ckidney = "Kidneys", Cpancreas = "Pancreas", Cspleen = "Spleen")

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = ev_typ, keep = "occasion"
) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_typ_long <- sim_typ |>
  select(id, time, occasion, all_of(names(tissues))) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(tissues)), names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(tissue = factor(tissues[output], levels = tissues))

ggplot(sim_typ_long, aes(time, conc, colour = occasion)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~tissue, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ug/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical-value profiles after 12.5 ug [11C]glibenclamide",
    caption = "Compare with the individual fits in Figure 4 of Comin 2025."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Mass balance

Without a sink other than `kel`, the amount still in the body plus the
cumulative elimination must equal the dose. The cumulative elimination is the
trapezoidal integral of `kel * central` on a fine grid, so the check is limited
only by quadrature error.

```{r mass-balance}
ev_mb <- make_events(1L, occ = 1L, rif = 0L) |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(
    id = 1L, time = seq(0, 3, by = 1 / 3600), amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L,
    cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, OCC = 1L, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN_SD = 0L
  ))

mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_mb) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    in_body = central + liver + liver_deep + kidney + kidney_deep + spleen + pancreas,
    elim_rate = exp(th[["lkel"]]) * central,
    eliminated = c(0, cumsum(diff(time) * (head(elim_rate, -1) + tail(elim_rate, -1)) / 2)),
    total = in_body + eliminated
  )

mb_err <- max(abs(mb$total[mb$time >= 0.1] - dose_ug)) / dose_ug
mb_err
stopifnot(mb_err < 0.005)
```

# Stochastic simulation (Supplementary Figure S2)

Supplementary Figure S2 is a prediction-corrected VPC with the 10th, 50th and
90th percentiles. The simulation below uses 200 virtual subjects per occasion,
each receiving the mean microdose of 12.5 ug, with between-subject and
residual variability.

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)
n_per_occ <- 200L
ev_vpc <- bind_rows(
  make_events(seq_len(n_per_occ), occ = 1L, rif = 0L) |>
    mutate(occasion = "Baseline"),
  make_events(n_per_occ + seq_len(n_per_occ), occ = 2L, rif = 1L) |>
    mutate(occasion = "Rifampicin")
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_vpc[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_vpc, keep = "occasion") |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, time, occasion, all_of(names(tissues))) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(tissues)), names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(tissue = factor(tissues[output], levels = tissues)) |>
  group_by(tissue, occasion, time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(conc, 0.10), p50 = quantile(conc, 0.50), p90 = quantile(conc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50, colour = occasion, fill = occasion)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~tissue, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ug/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles (IPRED)",
    caption = "Compare with Supplementary Figure S2 of Comin 2025."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# PKNCA: exposure over the 40-min acquisition

The paper does not tabulate NCA values. The companion non-compartmental
analysis of the same data (Marie et al., cited as reference 6) is quoted in the
Discussion as a blood AUC increase of +24 +/- 24% with rifampicin. PKNCA is run
below on the individual predictions (the `Cc` and `Cliver` columns that
`rxSolve` returns, which carry between-subject but not residual variability)
over the 0-40 min acquisition window, by occasion.

```{r pknca}
run_nca <- function(dat, output) {
  conc <- dat |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[output]])) |>
    transmute(id, occasion, time, conc = .data[[output]])
  conc <- bind_rows(
    conc,
    conc |> distinct(id, occasion) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)
  ) |>
    distinct(id, occasion, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, occasion, time)
  doses <- ev_vpc |>
    filter(evid == 1L) |>
    select(id, occasion, time, amt)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 40 / 60, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | occasion + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | occasion + id),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
}

nca_blood <- run_nca(sim, "Cc")
nca_liver <- run_nca(sim, "Cliver")

nca_summary <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_blood$result) |> mutate(tissue = "Blood"),
  as.data.frame(nca_liver$result) |> mutate(tissue = "Liver")
) |>
  group_by(tissue, occasion, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_summary |>
  select(tissue, occasion, cmax, tmax, auclast) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Tissue" = tissue, "Occasion" = occasion, "Cmax (ug/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-40min (ug*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Median simulated NCA over the 40-min acquisition (200 subjects per occasion).")

auc_ratio <- nca_summary |>
  select(tissue, occasion, auclast) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = occasion, values_from = auclast) |>
  mutate(pct_change = 100 * (Rifampicin / Baseline - 1))
knitr::kable(auc_ratio, digits = 2, caption = "Rifampicin effect on median AUC0-40min.")
```

The model-predicted blood AUC increase with rifampicin is within the
+24 +/- 24% range of the companion NCA, and the liver AUC falls by roughly half,
consistent with the paper's statement that the final model shows "a
significant reduction in hepatic radioactivity following OATP inhibition". The
checks below are deliberately loose: the two sides are a model prediction and
an independent NCA of observed data, and the blood comparison is between
medians of unpaired virtual cohorts.

```{r pknca-checks}
blood_change <- auc_ratio$pct_change[auc_ratio$tissue == "Blood"]
liver_change <- auc_ratio$pct_change[auc_ratio$tissue == "Liver"]
stopifnot(
  blood_change > 0, blood_change < 48,
  liver_change < -25, liver_change > -75
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Final model only.** The paper also reports the final model refitted with
  the SLCO1B1 CC subject (Supplementary Table S1), an alternative with spleen
  and pancreas as fixed ratios of blood (Table S2), and a blood + liver-only
  model (Table S3). These are sensitivity analyses and are not packaged.
- **IOV value read as an SD.** The paper states that the IOV on kL1B "was fixed
  at 0.01". Table 2 reports every other random effect as an SD (omega), as
  Monolix does, so 0.01 is taken as the SD and the model carries a variance of
  1e-4 on each of the two occasion-level random effects.
- **Concentration units.** The Methods text converts radioactivity to "ug/mL",
  but Table 2 gives the additive errors in ug/L, and the dose (about 12.5 ug)
  divided by the blood volume (3.6 L) gives concentrations of a few ug/L. The
  model uses ug for amounts, L for volumes and ug/L for concentrations.
- **Compartment count.** The abstract says the final model has seven
  compartments and the Results says six; the published equation system
  (Results equation 5) has seven states (blood, two liver, two kidney, spleen,
  pancreas), which is what is implemented.
- **Covariance.** Correlations between random effects were tested but none is
  reported in Table 2, so all random effects are independent.
- **Parent-drug signal.** As in the paper, the PET radioactivity is attributed
  entirely to parent glibenclamide; the authors note radiometabolites were
  below 10% of blood radioactivity by the end of acquisition.
- **Poorly identified spleen and pancreas parameters.** VS, kBS, VP and kBP
  have relative standard errors of order 1e5% in Table 2 and varied three- to
  eight-fold between estimation runs (Supplementary Figure S3). They are
  packaged as published; the concentration ratios they imply are better
  determined than the individual values.
- **Microdose.** The model describes the first 40 min after a microdose and
  the authors caution against extrapolating the elimination rate; it is not a
  model of therapeutic glibenclamide dosing.
- No correction notice for the article was found as of 2026-11-10.
